name: Naftali Bennett
role: Prime Minister of Israel (2021–2022); former Minister of Defense, Education, Economy and Diaspora Affairs; leader of Jewish Home, Yamina and, in 2026, the Beyachad (Together) list
summary: Israeli tech entrepreneur turned politician from the national-religious right. He opposes a Palestinian state and further withdrawals, voted for the Nation-State Basic Law, led the 2021–22 coalition of right, centre, left and an Arab party, and in 2026 campaigns on ending Haredi draft exemptions and state funding for those who neither serve nor work.

civil-marriage.rationale: He voted against the bills permitting civil marriage and civil divorce on 28 November 2018.

conscription.rationale: He treats compulsory military service as the standard to be enforced: in 2023 he said the law requiring Haredi men to serve or stay in yeshiva until 26 exists because it is unfair that others serve; in 2026 he demanded repeal of the draft-evasion law with 'no exceptions' and no quotas.

death-penalty.rationale: On 1 June 2022 he voted against sending the bill to impose the death penalty on terrorists to committee.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: In his UN speech he said 'it is vital that different people think differently' and 'we can debate without hate', that debate is the power of innovation.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: At Brookings he defended the Nation-State bill as protecting the Law of Return, which applies only to Jews, and Taglit-Birthright, against court petitions that they are unfair.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His 2026 party plan proposes a Basic Law: Equality guaranteeing equality before the law, and he told the 'Sagi Laws' conference 'You simply want the rights every Israeli deserves'.

gradual-change.rationale: In 2023 he urged being 'a bit more incrementalist' on Haredi work and service, expecting change in 20 to 25 years; in 2026 he said October 7 changed his view and called for ending funding at once: 'You have to grab the bull by the horns.'

history-own-civilization.rationale: At Brookings, closing his remarks, he said of the Jewish homeland 'I want every Israeli child to know our history'.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He voted for the Nation-State Basic Law, Basic Law: Israel – The Nation State of the Jewish People, on 19 July 2018.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: At Brookings he said restoring Jewish values does not mean theocracy: 'I'm not talking about, you know, forcing anything. I'm against any of those laws.'

more-religion-public.rationale: At Brookings he said Israel must 'restore the Jewish soul' and Jewish values (not theocracy or coercion), because Israel exists as the Jewish homeland and not merely as a shelter.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: In his 2014 New York Times op-ed he wrote that for its security 'Israel cannot withdraw from more territory and cannot allow for the establishment of a Palestinian state in the West Bank', citing the 1990s, 2000 and 2005 withdrawals; at Brookings he said the same.

patriotic-education.rationale: In 2026 he said Haredi pupils must not be taught against the State of Israel, Zionism and the IDF, and promised state Haredi schools teaching math and English that educate in favor of military service.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He called for restoring Jewish values and the Jewish soul to Israel at Brookings and describes Israel as the revival of an ancient nation, its language and sovereignty at the UN.

results-over-ideology.rationale: In his UN speech he described his pandemic approach as trial and error: 'When something works, we keep it. When it does not, we discard it and move on.'

revive-national-language.rationale: His UN speech counts the revival of the ancient Hebrew language, with the return to the homeland and restored sovereignty, among the achievements of Israel as 'a miracle of Jewish revival'.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2015 he stated 'Recognition – no; rights – yes' on same-sex marriage; his 2026 party plan offers a civil partnership with all the rights and obligations of married couples but does not use the term marriage, and the report says whether he supports same-sex marriage 'remains open'.

term-limits.rationale: One of his stated coalition terms in 2026 is 'a prime ministerial term limit of eight years'.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: His UN speech describes Israel as 'an ancient nation of people who have returned to our ancient homeland, revived our ancient language and restored our ancient sovereignty'; at Brookings he said of Jacob, 'He's my father... we spoke the same language, same land'.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In 2026 he said 'Anyone who does not work will not receive a shekel from the state', calling it the 'Brooklyn model' where a man who studies Torah and does not work is not funded.

notes: First pass, every statement answered (20 known, the rest null). His own words are two 2014 texts (Brookings transcript, New York Times op-ed), his 2021 UN speech, and 2023 and 2026 interviews reported by news outlets; the record is his Knesset plenum votes (all 3,988 read for the topics of the statements). He has no recorded position on most economic, government, ecology, technology and world-order statements: he has spoken on the Palestinian question, Iran, the Haredi draft, religion and state and LGBTQ rights, not on taxes, markets, regulation, trade or the environment. Where a vote and later words differ (civil marriage, death penalty) the answer follows the vote.
